From timesheet to invoice. Automated.

StaffFlow reads your consultants' timesheets, applies each client's billing rules and prepares invoices for your approval, then keeps everything checked against QuickBooks.

1. Receive timesheetPDF, Excel, photo or email body
2. Extract & readConsultant, dates and hours
3. Apply rulesClient, vendor, rates, calendars
4. You approveThe exact amount, before it bills
5. Invoice in QuickBooksCreated and tracked to payment
6. Track on dashboardRevenue, cash flow and status
Reads any timesheetPDFs, photos, Excel or the email body, straight from your inbox
Every billing cycleWeekly, biweekly, monthly and client calendars
Invoices you approveCreated in QuickBooks only after you approve the exact amount
Vendor portal paymentsTurns portal statements into invoices, as stated
Follows up automaticallyOverdue timesheets and reminders, with the exact dates owed
Reconciled every nightChecked against QuickBooks so edits never slip by
PayrollCash flowAudit trail

All reviews
Review & act on flagged items — confirm a billable label or resolve a checked item; held items can be discarded.
Billing choices you have already made on unbilled periods — reversible while the timesheet is unchanged. Decisions on billed periods are corrected via Correct Billed.
Activity log
Everything the pipeline did — emails received, held or failed, review resolutions, and invoices generated. Warnings flag anything that produced no result or needs a look.
Profit & Loss
Gross margin = revenue − consultant pay, before loaded costs. This does not yet include insurance, immigration, employer taxes, or benefits — true net margin will be lower. Revenue is net of VMS. Rows needing a pay rate are flagged, never counted as zero-cost.

Payroll
Hours are counted in the calendar month they fall in. Pay is 80% of the billed amount after VMS. How this is calculated
Pay hours are calendar-month — each day is counted in the month it falls in.
Pay = (hours × bill rate − VMS) × 80%.
For consultants billed by weekly or custom cadence this can differ from the billed amount by design — hover a on any row to see why.
A flagged row shows Pending review rather than a figure. It is never a partial amount.

Hours Tracking
Compare each consultant's hours against a full-time year, so a placement running light is visible before year-end. The target is a yardstick, not a contractual guarantee — nothing here is owed to anyone. Running below it is a signal to look, not a verdict: it can mean leave, a slow ramp, or seasonal work. Shown in hours; dollars appear only where a pay rate is set.

Verify against QuickBooks

The client’s business day. Every date on the dashboard — and every judgement about whether a period has closed — is answered in this timezone, whoever is looking.

Security
Dual-control approval
Require a second, different approver before invoices above a set amount can bill. A money-safety control for compliance — leave it off for solo billing.
Threshold $ invoices at or above this need two approvers
Every change is recorded — who, when and why. Turning the control off or lowering the threshold reduces a safety control and requires a reason.

Deactivate placement

Stops future billing and drops this consultant off the active roster. All history is kept, and you can reactivate later.

End date The last day this placement is active. Leave blank to use today.

Delete permanently

This permanently removes the placement and its rates. It only works for rows with no history (no timesheets, no invoices, no transition link). This cannot be undone.

Type the PL-code to confirm * Deleting a real consultant is almost never right — deactivate instead. This is for test rows and mistakes.
